newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: African coffee producers start export cut talks.
newsitem.headline: African coffee producers start export cut talks.

text.p: African coffee ministers opened talks in Ivory Coast on Thursday aimed at implementing robusta exports cuts agreed in January at a worldwide producers' meeting in Brazil.

African countries agreed after an Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) meeting in Rio de Janeiro to cut total robusta exports by 850,000 60-kilo bags between January and June 1997 in an attempt to force up prices.

"(The meeting) will reflect deeply on the world market situation and additional measures to be envisaged in order to consolidate the current price rally," said Arega Worku, Secretary-General of the Interafrican Coffee Organisation (IACO).
Details of export cuts by individual producers are not expected to be published.
African producers, which called for the emergency talks in Brazil as prices slumped in late 1996, consider upward price movement to be a result of export cut plans.
Robusta prices hit a nine month high of $1,820 on Wednesday before falling back to close at $1,780 basis May. It is currently trading at $1,737 a tonne.
"World coffee prices are now very satisfactory," said Worku.
Traders have pointed to other factors including supply uncertainty and stock inventory management policies.
IACO said only larger producers would be concerned by any cuts apportioned - including Uganda, Ivory Coast, Cameroon, Kenya, Zaire, Tanzania, Madagascar and Ethiopia.
World market trends, robusta production by non-IACO countries and IACO budget deficits were also on the agenda, said Worku.
Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze, Chairman of 25-member IACO, was abroad on Thursday and expected to attend from Friday morning at the latest.
Colombia, Brazil and Indonesia representatives have been invited.
